AraRooPat Explainer

An Arabic word carries its meaning in a three-consonant root and its grammar in a pattern. This tokenizer splits them into two symbols and hands them to LLaMA-3.2-1B. Follow one sentence all the way through — and watch where it breaks.

Real traces, precomputed. Every analysis, token id, embedding, attention map and logit on this page came from running the tokenizer against a live CAMeL Tools bridge and a fine-tuned checkpoint — vocab 3,784, model 981M params. Nothing here is illustrative.

01

Input, cut into runs

The tokenizer never treats a whitespace word as atomic. It walks the characters and cuts wherever the class changes — Arabic letter, digit, punctuation, or other. Click any word to drive every panel below it.

Character-class runs

alpha is the 35 letters of ARABIC_LETTERS plus 12 diacritics. Anything else — Latin, emoji, and notably ى — is other and becomes <unk>.

This head's attention

Attention matrix

Row i queries, column j is a key it attends to; causal, so the upper triangle is empty. Look for a pattern token attending to its root — that is the model composing the word.

Head stack

Heads concatenated → o_proj → residual add

SwiGLU feed-forward

Two projections run in parallel on the same input. gate passes through SiLU and gates up elementwise — this is what replaces GPT-2's single GELU MLP. Strips sample 32 of the 8,192 intermediate channels.

Next-token distribution at the final position

Re-softmaxed live from the stored top-400 logits, exactly as the sampler would. Notice how much of the mass sits on pattern tokens: the model learned the class grammar of the vocabulary.
06

Back to Arabic

Decoding is a single left-to-right pass over four registers. Dispatch is on the token's string prefix — which is exactly why proclitics and enclitics carry different prefixes, so the decoder knows which way a clitic attaches.

clitic_prefix
pending_root
out

Three-tier reconstruction

TIER 1 Lookup table — observed (root, pattern) pairs. O(1), hits ≈99 % of emissions.
TIER 2 CAMeL generator: naive-fill, re-analyse the rough form, return the matching stem. Recovers قال where substitution gives قَوَلَ.
TIER 3 Naive slot substitution. Always available, wrong on weak roots.

Why words miss the morphology path

Measured over 2,535 word occurrences of real benchmark Arabic, before the 2026-08-30 fix. CAMeL writes # where a root radical is weak — قال · يقول · قول · أقوال all analyse as ق.#.ل — and the code stripped it, then rejected the shortened root. That discarded half the corpus, weak roots being among the commonest words in the language. What changed →

Token classes in real text

Only 22 % of words reached root + pattern, at 5.43 tokens per word — the character path, not the design, was what you were mostly looking at. After the fixes it is 48.2 % at 4.39. What changed →

What changed — 2026-08-30

Everything above traces araroopat_balanced, the artifact as it was. Two defects it exposed have since been fixed, and they had to be fixed together.

1 — the # radical is kept. It marks a radical whose surface form is not stable across the paradigm, and it is complementary to the pattern: the masked slot digit is absent from the pattern and the realized letter sits there as literal template material (1ا3َ · يَ1ُو3 · 1َوْ3ِ). Verified on 457 of 457 masked radicals, zero counter-examples. Deleting it dropped the root below the three-radical bar and renumbered the survivors so the pattern's slots indexed the wrong letters. Roots are now counted structurally and [ROOT_ق#ل] is a legal token.

2 — the pattern budget was the real bottleneck. Keeping # moves the weak letter's identity out of the root and into the pattern, so unique patterns grew 8,634 → 21,578 while roots barely moved. At the old max_patterns: 500 the first fix delivered almost nothing. Budget re-tiered to 4,000 patterns; max_roots was never binding (only 4,128 roots qualify).

3 — the لِ + الـ contraction. Arabic writes one lam, not two: لِ + الوَلَد → لِلوَلَد. The article's surface is ل, not ال, so stripping it literally failed and left a stray lam in the bare pattern and the stem — 2,608 duplicate patterns out of 21,578, and للولد decoding as لالولد. Pre-existing and independent of the other two (it hits sound roots too); surfaced by the extra traffic they put on the morphological path. Encode and decode now implement the rule as inverses.

The metric was also measuring the wrong thing. morpheme_integrity_rate and clitic_separation_accuracy read 1.0 for this tokenizer, which looked like an architectural ceiling. It was not: both need the cleaned tokens to concatenate back into the word, which ROOT+PAT output never does (0 of 112 such words align; 488 of 488 character-path words do). They described the fallback path only. Five diagnostics now ship alongside — root_measurable_pct (~84 %, the share of words whose root is recoverable from the surface at all: قال does not contain the و of قول), root_conservation_attainable, morph_alignment_coverage, morph_alignment_ceiling and root_extractor_agreement. The first thing they caught: after the fix, coverage fell 0.43 → 0.21 while both rates kept printing 1.0.

Still open: CAMeL analyses 66.6 % of word occurrences and the tokenizer now admits 48.2 %; the rest is budget truncation with diminishing returns. The remaining third is CAMeL's backoff analyzer, which no budget reaches. Downstream accuracy impact is not yet measured — that needs a full 3-phase re-run against the archived experiment.
